scope: Post-archive ship verdict for release v0.4.5 at head e50c69cf — the closure PR edge (feature/0.4.5 -> develop) and the develop -> main deploy edge. REVIEWED RANGE: git diff c0b2080c..e50c69cf — 3 commits, 24 files, +24/-10, SPECS-ONLY, proven not assumed: git diff --name-only over the range, reduced to top-level path prefixes, yields exactly one prefix, 'specs'. Zero paths under dadaia_workspace/, .github/, tests/; zero dependency or lockfile lines; no Dockerfile, compose or Terraform input. The three commits are (1) e0c52527 marker close of T-045-35, (2) 15b778bf CLOSURE/TASKS amendments closing T-045-36 with zero rounds and routing the QA ancestor-symlink finding to intake, (3) e50c69cf the archive move of specs/releases/v0.4.5 into specs/_archive/releases/v0.4.5 plus ACTIVE.md phase CLOSURE -> ARCHIVED. ARCHIVE-MOVE INTEGRITY, MEASURED PER PATH: of the 22 relocated files, 20 are byte-identical relocations (blob sha at the parent equals blob sha at the archived path, so git republishes no object) and 2 are NEW blobs at the archived path — CLOSURE.md and TASKS.md — because the same commit also amended them. The move is therefore NOT a pure rename; the exact deltas are enumerated in the LOW finding and are closure prose plus two marker flips, nothing else. PRIVACY LANE: the whole added surface is 24 lines, swept for home-absolute POSIX and Windows user paths, e-mail literals, IPv4 and IPv6 literals, internal hostname shapes, assignment-shaped credential literals, PEM private-key blocks, cloud and CI key prefixes, bearer or authorization headers, and every foreign repo slug in the workspace registry — 0 hits in every class. The two NEW archive blobs were swept whole, not only their added lines, because an archive-authored document carries no published prior text at its new path and therefore receives no amnesty from the push scan. PUBLICATION BOUNDARY REPLAYED, NOT SIMULATED: origin/feature/0.4.5 is at c0b2080c (git ls-remote), so the real push range equals the reviewed range; dadaia ci push-gate-check fed the real refspec on stdin reports mode 'operator denylist + baseline' and exits 0, and the repository self-scan sentinel (tests/integration/test_repo_self_scan.py, the check that scans an archive-prefixed path iff its blob is new at HEAD) is 5 passed at this head. GATE-POSTURE LANE: ACTIVE.md phase ARCHIVED is a canonical phase token and closes memory writes fail-closed; the verdict gate no longer reads that pointer at all and resolves evidence by artifact glob over both the live and the archived verdicts trees, which the RED baseline run at this head demonstrates by reading all six relocated verdict files before refusing.
verdict_reason: No CRITICAL, HIGH or MEDIUM finding. The range is specs-only: zero production modules, zero CLI, zero gate, hook or workflow, zero test files, zero dependency lines, zero infrastructure-as-code input — so no executed path, no gate predicate, no matcher and no dependency changed, and the production security posture at e50c69cf is byte-identical to the posture approved at 0d219434. None of the mandatory REQUEST_CHANGES triggers is present: no secret or token, no PII, no public-asset privacy violation, no auth or access-control change, no unsafe dependency addition, no generated-file leakage, no deploy leakage, no consumer-specific data exposure. The privacy question the operator posed was answered mechanically rather than by reading: all 24 added lines are clean in every scanned class, and the real refspec c0b2080c..e50c69cf was replayed through the actual pre-push denylist scan (exit 0, zero offending objects) rather than reasoned about — this matters more than usual here, because the archive commit publishes two blobs that were never published before, and the FROZEN-to-scan invariant grants an archive path no amnesty precisely so that case is scanned like any other new object. The one deviation found is recorded as LOW and is a record-integrity observation, not a vulnerability: the archive commit is a relocation for 20 of 22 files but authors two new blobs at archived paths, so the auditable property 'an archived release's bytes are the bytes its closure verdicts reviewed' does not hold for CLOSURE.md and TASKS.md. Both deltas are benign in content and both were scanned; git records no write order, so whether the amendment happened before or after the move — the difference between lawful authoring at the live path and an edit of a FROZEN path — is not decidable from history, which is itself the reportable part. Bug-surface axis (FR24): the ledger blob specs/bugs/bugs.jsonl is byte-identical at 18638d3b, 0d219434, c0b2080c and e50c69cf, and git log over the range restricted to specs/bugs/ and specs/backlog/ is empty, so this range neither opened nor closed a bug; folding the ledger at this head gives 495 distinct bugs and exactly 1 open (windows-xdist-workers-crash-on-unit-fast-tier), unchanged from the prior verdict's head. Bug surface direction: UNCHANGED for production (zero production lines, zero branches, zero flags, zero new code paths) and UNCHANGED for tests (zero test files). The diff direction is not accretion: it closes markers and records outcomes, and the one substantive addition — intake item 16 for the symlinked-ancestor finding — routes a HIGH QA finding to the operator's demand queue instead of bolting a special case onto the FR8 refusal, which is the correct structural call given that refusing every symlinked ancestor would break macOS temp-path resolution. The prior verdict's open findings covering 18638d3b (one MEDIUM plus LOW and INFO items) are not re-litigated here and carry forward to the deploy edge unchanged.

findings.message: Scan summary — specs-only range (3 commits, 24 files, +24/-10) proven by path class; three of five lanes have zero input, and the two that do were replayed against the real refspec.
findings.detail_md:
**Target.** `git diff c0b2080c..e50c69cf` — 3 commits, 24 files, +24 / -10.

| commit | subject | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `e0c52527` | close T-045-35 | one marker flip in `TASKS.md` (`[-]` to `[x]`) |
| `15b778bf` | close T-045-36 with zero rounds | `CLOSURE.md` +11/-4, `TASKS.md` one marker flip; records the merged rc-1, and routes the QA ancestor-symlink HIGH to intake as candidate item 16 |
| `e50c69cf` | archive v0.4.5 | 22 paths move to `specs/_archive/releases/v0.4.5/`, `ACTIVE.md` phase `CLOSURE` to `ARCHIVED`, two markers flip |

**Specs-only, proven:** the changed-path list reduced to top-level prefixes yields exactly one entry, `specs`. Zero paths under `dadaia_workspace/`, `.github/` or `tests/`; `git diff` restricted to `pyproject.toml` and `poetry.lock` returns 0 lines.

**Lane inputs.** OWASP: no executed path, no auth or access-control surface, no injection sink, no deserialization, no SSRF surface — the only security-relevant structure touched is the verdict-evidence tree itself, covered in its own finding. CVE and supply chain: 0 dependency, extra, constraint or lockfile lines — no input. Infrastructure-as-code: no workflow, Dockerfile, compose or Terraform path — no input. Secrets and privacy: 24 added lines plus two whole new archive blobs — see the privacy finding. Publication boundary: replayed, see below.

**Publication boundary, replayed on the real refspec.** `git ls-remote` puts `origin/feature/0.4.5` at `c0b2080c`, so the range under review IS the range the next push would publish. Feeding the real pre-push ref line to `dadaia ci push-gate-check` prints `[pre-push] denylist scan mode: operator denylist + baseline` and exits **0**. The repository self-scan sentinel — the check that scans an archive-prefixed path iff its blob is new at HEAD — is **5 passed** at this head.

findings.message: The archive commit is NOT a pure rename: 20 of 22 relocated files are byte-identical relocations, but CLOSURE.md and TASKS.md are authored anew at the archived path in the same commit.
findings.detail_md:
**Measured per path, not inferred from the rename score.** Comparing each blob sha at the parent `15b778bf` (live path) against the archived path at `e50c69cf`:

| path | parent blob | archived blob | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SPEC.md` | `d85fa45c` | `d85fa45c` | identical |
| `PLAN.md` | `003ee96f` | `003ee96f` | identical |
| 12 files under `reviews/` | — | — | identical (12/12) |
| 6 files under `verdicts/` | — | — | identical (6/6) |
| `CLOSURE.md` | `dd2bcc47` | `378717bd` | **new blob** |
| `TASKS.md` | `43bd7545` | `0b2d76f0` | **new blob** |

`git show --name-status --find-renames=100% e50c69cf` agrees: those two paths report as `A` plus `D`, every other path as `R100`.

**The exact deltas** (nothing else differs):

1. `CLOSURE.md`, section *Ship-without-publish record* — a 7-line 'Where V12 lands' paragraph stating that the directory is archived and `specs/_archive/` is FROZEN, so the three A16.8 verifications will be recorded as a `note` record in the live release's `RELEASE.jsonl` instead, plus the sentence 'This section originally read:' prefixed to the pre-existing text (content preserved, not replaced).
2. `TASKS.md` — two marker flips: T-045-39 `[ ]` to `[x]`, T-045-40 `[ ]` to `[-]`.

**Why this is recorded and why it is LOW.** `DADAIA.md` section 3 classes `specs/_archive/` FROZEN — 'archive by `git mv`, never edit' — and the `sdd-gate-v3` memory atom's FROZEN-to-scan invariant is argued from that premise: relocating unchanged bytes republishes no object, so an already-published term is amnestied by construction. The same atom explicitly contemplates the other case and calls it correct behaviour: 'A document *authored* into `specs/_archive/` — a `CLOSURE.md` written at close time, a QA artifact created in place — is an ordinary new blob: its content has never been published, the archive path grants it nothing, and the scan reads it like any other new object.' That is exactly what happened, and the scan did read them: the push-gate replay over the real refspec exits 0 and the self-scan sentinel is green, so no amnesty was needed and none was granted. Nothing leaked.

**What is actually lost** is an audit property, not a control: for these two files, 'the archived bytes are the bytes the closure verdicts reviewed' no longer holds. And git records no write ORDER — editing at the live path and then moving (lawful, the gate never sees an archive write) produces the identical commit to moving and then editing (a FROZEN-path write the SDD gate would refuse for a file tool, though a `Bash` heredoc is outside that gate's parsing). History cannot distinguish them, which is the reportable part.
findings.fix_recommendation: project-manager plus product-engineer, off this PR edge: rule once whether closure prose authored into the archived directory in the same commit as the move is sanctioned cadence. If it is, say so in the `sdd-gate-v3` atom, whose invariant is currently written as 'it is never edited' — the sanctioned-authoring paragraph two paragraphs later already contradicts the absolute, and a future reader deciding whether a fix is needed will hit the contradiction first. If it is not, the mechanical cheap fix is ordering: amend the file at the live path, then `git mv`, so the archive commit stays a pure relocation and the invariant holds literally. No change requested on this branch.

findings.message: Verdict-evidence chain survives the move intact: all six prior verdict handoffs relocated byte-identically, and the gate proved it resolves them by artifact glob in the archived tree.
findings.detail_md:
The six files under `specs/_archive/releases/v0.4.5/verdicts/` are byte-identical relocations (6/6 blob shas unchanged), so no prior verdict was rewritten, weakened or dropped by the archive move — the tamper question a relocation of review evidence always raises is answered by content addressing, not by trust.

**The gate reads them where they now live.** Running the real gate backend at this head before this verdict existed — `PR_HEAD_SHA=e50c69cf... RELEASE_ID=v0.4.5 bash .github/scripts/pr-verdict-check.sh` — enumerates all six archived candidates, parses each, and refuses with exit **1**: five are APPROVED but no longer cover the head (the archive move itself is the intervening non-verdict diff), and one is the REJECTED verdict at `5a8810ac`, correctly skipped by the qualification fields rather than by a path rule. That is the RED baseline this verdict exists to clear, and it doubles as proof that the post-archive resolution path (the fix for bug `verdict-gate-cannot-resolve-evidence-after-release-archive`) works at this head: evidence resolves by artifact, never by asking `ACTIVE.md` which release is active — which matters precisely here, because this range set that pointer to `ARCHIVED`.
findings.fix_recommendation: None — record-only; the RED-then-GREEN pair is the evidence that this verdict is required rather than ceremonial.

**Whole-blob sweep, not just added lines.** Because `CLOSURE.md` and `TASKS.md` enter the archive as NEW blobs (see the LOW finding), the push scan reads them entire and grants them no amnesty — the amnesty rule suppresses a candidate only when the exact matched value already appears in the SAME path's published prior text, and these archived paths have no published prior text at all. Both files were therefore swept whole: 0 hits in every class above.

**Mechanical confirmation.** `dadaia ci push-gate-check` on the real refspec `c0b2080c..e50c69cf`: mode `operator denylist + baseline`, exit **0**, zero offending objects — the operator denylist layer active, so the check covers operator-private terms this reviewer never sees in plaintext.
findings.fix_recommendation: None — nothing to redact; recorded so the zero is checkable rather than asserted.

findings.message: Gate posture after `phase: ARCHIVED` is fail-closed, not fail-open: the token is canonical and memory writes stop.
findings.detail_md:
The single mutating line outside the move is `specs/releases/ACTIVE.md`: `phase: CLOSURE` becomes `phase: ARCHIVED`. Two checks, because a phase string feeds the SDD gate:

1. **Token validity.** `ARCHIVED` is a member of `CANONICAL_PHASES` in `features/specs/doctor_release.py` — not an unrecognized value the gate would have to interpret.
2. **Direction of the change.** `features/spec_context/gate_policy.py` allows a MEMORY-class write only when the phase is `DEFINITION` or `CLOSURE`; every other value, `ARCHIVED` included, refuses with the RULE A message naming the current phase. So the transition CLOSES a write class rather than opening one — the correct posture for a release whose memory window is finished, and the opposite of a fail-open.

The verdict gate itself no longer consults this pointer (that read was removed when `verdict-gate-cannot-resolve-evidence-after-release-archive` was fixed), so setting it to `ARCHIVED` cannot re-open the ungateable-PR hole that bug described.

findings.message: The four `specs doctor` errors at this head are pre-existing tooling-version skew against a v0.4.5-era memory tree, not a regression introduced by this range.
findings.detail_md:
`dadaia specs doctor` pointed at this branch's own `specs/` reports 4 errors and 10 warnings: three `SPEC-DOC-002` (missing `memory/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `memory/TECHSTACK.md`, `memory/QUALITY.md`) and one `LINT-1` (wikilink lint on `memory/architecture.md`).

**Not caused by this range.** `git ls-tree specs/memory/` is byte-identical at `c0b2080c` and at `e50c69cf` — this branch carries the v0.4.5-era names `architecture.md`, `tech-stack.md`, `quality-assurance.md`, while the installed CLI is the later build that expects the renamed atoms. The range touches no file under `specs/memory/`.

Recorded so this is not mistaken for damage from the archive move, and so nobody 'fixes' a v0.4.5 branch to satisfy a doctor from a later canon. Note for the same reason that `dadaia bugs status` and an unscoped `specs doctor` resolve to the bound context's checkout, not to this worktree — every ledger and doctor figure in this verdict was computed against this branch's own tree explicitly.
findings.fix_recommendation: None on this edge — informational. The skew resolves when this branch merges forward.

findings.message: Bug-surface axis (FR24): UNCHANGED in both directions — the ledger blob is byte-identical across the whole range, and the one substantive addition routes a finding to intake instead of growing a feature.
findings.detail_md:
**Ledger, measured.** `specs/bugs/bugs.jsonl` has blob sha `3e08088b` at `18638d3b`, `0d219434`, `c0b2080c` AND `e50c69cf` — unchanged since well before this range. `git log c0b2080c..e50c69cf -- specs/bugs/ specs/backlog/` is empty. Folding this branch's ledger at this head: 1016 records, 495 distinct bugs, exactly **1 open** — `windows-xdist-workers-crash-on-unit-fast-tier`, the same single open bug the prior verdict named. This range neither opened nor closed a bug and exercised no redaction surface.

**Production surface:** +0 lines, +0 branches, +0 flags, +0 code paths. It cannot increase the bug surface of any feature.

**Structural direction (permanent architecture review, oriented by bug history).** The one substantive addition is intake candidate 16, `specs-init-symlinked-ancestor-refusal`: QA found on the merged `develop` that `specs init --specs-dir` follows a symlinked ANCESTOR, while the accepted FR8 refusal (A8.1) covers the literal target. The closure records it as needing design and explicitly refuses the reflex fix — refusing any symlinked ancestor would break macOS, where the system temp path is itself a link, so the check must be scoped to links inside the workspace tree. Routing it to the operator's demand queue rather than bolting a second predicate onto the live refusal is the correct call: it is a real CWE-59-class gap, but the fix is a scoping decision, not a branch to add during closure. The residual risk while it sits in intake is bounded — it needs an attacker-controlled symlinked ancestor of a path the operator passes to `specs init` — and it is now written down where the next agent reading the ledger will find it, which is where the prior verdict's LOW finding said such hypotheses belong.
findings.fix_recommendation: project-manager: carry candidate 16 into the intake report so the operator can decide it; qa-engineer's handoff carries the reproduction. No action on this edge.
